subject: DPA / data flows: retention window, subprocessors & evidence request
messages:
From: Anya Patel <anya@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: DPA questions — data flows, retention windows, subprocessors

Hi Diego,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Acme Health is doing an internal compliance pass and we have a few DPA/security questions we need to close before we can proceed with a pilot. Attached is our questionnaire and a proposed dataflow sketch. High level items we need clarified:

- Which subprocessors handle unredacted PII (name, MRN, DOB)?
- Where are tokens and logs stored (region)? EU residency requirement applies to some workloads.
- Do you support customer-managed KMS for key separation and can you attest to no-export policy?
- Retention: can you support a 90-day retention for request logs and configurable longer retention for governance records (up to 7 years)?
- Evidence: SOC 2 report, access matrix, and a redlined dataflow for our archive process.

I've attached: acme-security-questionnaire-v2.xlsx and acme-dataflow-proposal.vsdx — please let me know if you prefer a short call to walk through.

Thanks,
Anya
Anya Patel
Senior InfoSec Manager, Acme Health
anya@acmehealth.com
security@acmehealth.com

From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood-inference.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@acmehealth.com>
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — data flows, retention windows, subprocessors

Hi Anya — thanks for the detailed packet. I'm Diego on the trust/security partnership team; happy to coordinate. High level answers below and a few follow-ups so we can produce the evidence you need.

Summary answers (high level):
- Subprocessors: we operate a small, public subprocessors list and can provide your team a CSV export of the vendors that may touch PII. Critical note: only the serving runtime and object storage subprocessors may see unredacted request bodies for hosted deployments; dedicated/private deployments reduce that surface.
- Regions and storage: by default hosted data resides in customer-selected cloud regions (we currently support eu-west-1, us-east-1, europe-west2). Logs (request traces) are retained by default 30 days; we support configurable retention windows for customers and can extend to 90 days for logs and 7 years for governance records under contract.
- KMS: we support customer-managed KMS in hosted (AWS KMS / GCP Cloud KMS) and HSM-backed key management in Private deployments. We do not provide plaintext key export for hosted managed keys; customer-managed KMS keeps control of key material.
- Evidence: we can share our most recent SOC 2 Type II report, a redacted access matrix, and a dataflow diagram that shows encryption and routing.

Follow-ups needed from Acme:
1) Confirm which workloads must be EU-resident vs. can be routed cross-border.
2) Confirm exact retention requirements per data category (PII request payloads, request logs, evaluation traces, audit logs).
3) Whether you require prior approval for new subprocessors (we have an approval SLA/process we can include in the DPA).

I've attached our internal dataflow (redwood-dataflow-v1.pdf) to illustrate where KV cache and logs live in the hosted model. Can I loop in our security lead and legal to prepare the DPA language and the subprocessor CSV?

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Trust & Security Partner, Redwood Inference
diego@redwood-inference.com

From: Anya Patel <anya@acmehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: security@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 05 Oct 2026 14:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — data flows, retention windows, subprocessors

Thanks Diego — quick clarifications:
- All EHR-derived payloads for pilot MUST remain in EU regions. Non-EHR telemetry can be cross-border.
- Retention (by data type):
  * Request payloads (PII): purge after 7 days unless explicitly archived under contract.
  * Request logs (traces/metadata): 90 days for operational purposes.
  * Governance/audit records: up to 7 years.
- We do require visibility and a 10-business-day notification window for new subprocessors plus the ability to review SOC/attestations for any subprocessor that may touch unredacted PII.

I've attached an evidence checklist (evidence-checklist.csv) that maps the rows in your questionnaire to the artifacts we expect. Happy to do a 30-min call if easier.

Regards,
Anya

From: Monica Patel <monica@redwood-inference.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@acmehealth.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood-inference.com>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — data flows, retention windows, subprocessors

Hi Anya — Monica from Redwood Security here. Looping in a few artifacts to close your checklist quickly.

What I'm attaching/providing now:
- redwood-subprocessors-2026-09.csv — current list of subprocessors and classification (serving, logging, monitoring). Any subprocessor flagged as "serving" may touch request payloads for hosted flows.
- SOC2-type2-2026.pdf (redacted) — our most recent Type II report.
- Short answers inline: we can support EU-only routing for specified workloads (we pin serving to region).
- Key management: hosted customers can register and use their own KMS keys (AWS/GCP); Private deployments can use HSMs. We do not perform key exports for customer-managed keys.

On subprocessors and approvals: our standard practice is a 10-business-day notification window and we provide vendor attestations on request. If Acme requires explicit written approval per vendor that handles PII, we can include that clause in an addendum (turnaround times vary depending on vendor NDA).

Attaching: redwood-subprocessors-2026-09.csv, SOC2-type2-2026.pdf

—Monica Patel
Head of Security Operations, Redwood Inference
monica@redwood-inference.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood-inference.com>
To: Anya Patel <anya@acmehealth.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood-inference.com>, Diego Fernandez <diego@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 06 Oct 2026 13:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: DPA questions — data flows, retention windows, subprocessors

Hi Anya — Rishi from Legal. Thanks for the clear requirements — below is proposed contract language for the retention and subprocessor approval items you raised. I'll attach a draft addendum for your in-house counsel to review.

1) Retention. Proposed clause: "Redwood shall delete or render unrecoverable Customer PII request payloads within seven (7) calendar days of ingestion for EU-only workloads, unless Customer explicitly directs retention for an archival purpose in writing. Request logs (metadata) shall be retained for ninety (90) days for operational purposes and may be retained longer with Customer consent. Governance and audit records may be retained up to seven (7) years as required by law."

2) Subprocessor approvals. Proposed clause: "Redwood shall maintain a public list of subprocessors and shall provide Customer with at least ten (10) business days prior written notice before engaging a new subprocessor that may access unredacted Customer PII. Customer shall have the right to reasonably review (and request clarifications) of subprocessor attestations; material objections may be subject to negotiated mitigation or substitution."

3) Cross-border transfers. We propose an Appendix referencing the EU SCCs (or equivalent transfer mechanism) and will supply a Data Transfer Addendum upon execution.

Attaching: dpa-addendum-draft.docx

If the above looks fine we can convert into a HubSpot deal task and propose a mutual action plan.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
rishi@redwood-inference.com

Diego / Monica / Rishi — thank you, that set is very helpful and addresses most of our asks. A few follow-ups:

- Please mark EU-only pinning for the three pilot projects and confirm in writing the region assignments.
- Please provide the redacted access matrix (who at Redwood has console access to logs and production clusters).
- Can we get the mutual action plan (dates for sign-off, SOC evidence delivery, and DPA execution)? Our legal would like the addendum draft in Word (you attached DOCX, good).

If possible, let's schedule a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize the MAP and confirm the subprocessor review cadence.

Thanks — Anya
